subject: BridgeWire integration — technical validation & reference design review
messages:
From: Alex Hayes <alex.hayes@bridgewire.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: integration validation & reference design review for BridgeWire <> Redwood

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the intro last week. BridgeWire is an ISV that builds adaptive data enrichment pipelines — we're onboarding a pilot customer and want to validate a production-ready reference integration with Redwood.

Attached is our initial reference design (BridgeWire-redwood-integration-v0.9.pdf). High-level asks:
- Quick architecture review to confirm compatibility with Redwood's serving runtime and caching semantics
- A short test plan for a smoke validation and perf targets (tokens/sec, p95 latency)
- Any security or cert requirements we should know about for private deployments (VPC / customer-managed keys)

Our ideal timeline is: design sync next week, validation tests the week after. We can provide a sandbox tenant and sample API keys.

Would love to schedule a 45-minute call with your solutions/partner team to walk through the design and agree on acceptance criteria.

Best,
Alex Hayes
Head of Integrations, BridgeWire
alex.hayes@bridgewire.io
+1 415 555 0217

Attachment: BridgeWire-redwood-integration-v0.9.pdf (pdf)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hayes <alex.hayes@bridgewire.io>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: integration validation & reference design review for BridgeWire <> Redwood

Thanks Alex — this looks like a good fit for a reference integration. Looping in Sergio (partner lead) and Marissa (solutions engineering) to own the technical validation.

High level proposal:
1) Design review (30–45m): confirm model variants, routing policy, and auth flows.
2) Compatibility checklist: endpoint semantics, streaming vs non-streaming, callback handling, and KV cache expectations.
3) Smoke validation: e2e test harness against a Redwood sandbox with a small workload (1–5 qps) and sample prompts.
4) Performance validation: run a short throughput test to capture p50/p95 latency and tokens/s.
5) Security review: confirm KMS/HSM requirements, TLS/cert pinning, and data retention flags for the pilot.

Preliminary acceptance criteria (to iterate):
- Successful end-to-end request/response for 95% of the test cases
- p95 latency under 800ms for the sample prompts during the smoke test
- No uncaught errors when routing fallbacks to a compatible model variant

Questions for you before the call:
- Can you provide a sandbox tenant and a small corpus of representative prompts (anonymized)?
- Do you plan to use webhook callbacks for result delivery, or will you poll?

Proposed times for the design sync: Tue 6/1 10:00–10:45 PT or Wed 6/2 14:00–14:45 PT. Please confirm what works and we'll send the invite.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Partner Solutions 
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: integration validation & reference design review for BridgeWire <> Redwood

Alex — happy to drive the runbook and the smoke tests. Attached is a lightweight runbook and checklist I typically use for partner validations (RW-BridgeWire-integration-runbook-v1.md and integration-acceptance-checklist.xlsx).

Quick engineering notes ahead of the call:
- Auth: we prefer JWT bearer between BridgeWire and the Redwood private control plane for dedicated/private deployments. If you need webhook callbacks, ensure the callback URL supports TLS 1.2+ and we recommend validating SANs on the cert.
- Streams: if you expect streaming tokens, we'll validate streaming hooks and fallbacks (we'll need to know if you plan to re-assemble partial streams server-side).
- Data flow: mark any PII in the sample corpus; we'll treat flagged tokens per the pilot's retention policy.
- Perf: for throughput tests please provide a 10-minute steady-state script and a ramp profile (we'll run 3 repeats).

Test cases (top-level):
- Auth success / auth failure handling
- Full request/response with streaming enabled
- Callback delivery and retry logic (3xx/5xx resilience)
- Fallback to smaller model under constrained capacity
- Latency under load (p95 target)

I'll prep a shared test harness and a LightHouse script to exercise these. Can you confirm what sandbox credentials you'll share and whether the pilot tenant is in us-west-2?

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Great — thanks Marissa. Alex, we locked Tue 6/8 10:00 PT for the design review with SE and product. Agenda will be: 1) design walkthrough (15m) 2) acceptance criteria and checklist (15m) 3) test plan and timeline (15m).

I created a Jira ticket to track technical tasks: PRT-4332. Also added the design and runbook to a shared drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/share/drive/1a2b3c/bridgewire-design-v0.9.

For the sandbox: please send the API key to marissa.cole@redwood.ai and grant a read/write sandbox tenant scoped to the BW-pilot org. We have a short-lived test key rotation policy — we'll need keys valid for at least 10 days from the start of testing.

Note on acceptance criteria: we'll run the smoke script Marissa attached and expect p95 < 800ms for the sample prompts during the controlled run. If we see regression between runs we'll investigate model selection / batching config.

Next steps:
- Alex: share sandbox credentials and sample prompts by EOD 6/4
- Marissa: prep test harness and first-run scripts by 6/6
- Jonas: coordinate design review invite and produce acceptance checklist in Jira

Thanks — Jonas

Team — quick update from our side after running the first smoke pass in the sandbox. Summary: most tests passed, we hit two minor issues we want to triage before the design review.

Findings summary:
- Callback delivery: our webhook client saw a mixed set of CORS headers on preflight responses; causes intermittent callback failures in browsers during local integration tests.
- TLS: one of our internal test hosts returned a certificate chain with an unexpected intermediate CA for the callback endpoint; browsers flagged the endpoint but server-to-server calls still worked.

Attached: bridgewire-smoke-results-20270603.txt with logs and a short checklist. We'll bring both items to the design review — they look fixable, but wanted to surface them early.

Thanks for the quick turnaround on scheduling. See you Tue 6/8.

Best,
Alex
Head of Integrations, BridgeWire
